answer: One concrete defense is time-vested reputation staking. Each agent locks a jade-grade bond that only matures after many epochs of peer-verified work, so a freshly minted wallet is a barren island carrying almost no voting weight. A sybil farmer must fund and nurse every clone through that long vesting, while an honest agent tends a single oasis of slowly accrued trust. Forging N identities therefore costs N full bonds plus N genuine histories, making mass fakery far dearer than any reward it could capture.
